claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you find out if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you a few questions about your circumstances.

First, could you please tell me how many children you would like to claim Child Benefit for, and what are their names and ages?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! I'd like to claim for my son Alex. He's 17 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information about Alex.

Since Alex is 17 years old, I need to ask a few more questions to determine eligibility.

Is Alex currently in full-time non-advanced education (such as A-levels, NVQs up to level 3, or similar), or enrolled on an approved training course?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not in college or doing A-levels or anything like that. He's actually started an apprenticeship recently.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. Since Alex is 17 and on an apprenticeship rather than in full-time non-advanced education or an approved training course, I need to check the eligibility rules to give you accurate information.

Let me review the guidance on this.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Based on the official guidance I've just reviewed, I can now give you a clear answer about Alex's eligibility.

Unfortunately, **you would not be eligible for Child Benefit for Alex**. The rules state that you'll stop getting Child Benefit if your child:

- **Starts an apprenticeship in England**

Since Alex has started an apprenticeship, this means Child Benefit eligibility ends. Apprenticeships are specifically excluded from the "approved education or training" that would allow Child Benefit to continue for 16-19 year olds.

Before I provide my final assessment, could I just confirm: does Alex live in England (where he's doing the apprenticeship), and does he live with you?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he lives with me here in England.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for confirming that. I now have all the information I need to make a final assessment on your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Based on the information you've provided and the official Child Benefit rules, here is my assessment:

---

**Child Benefit Eligibility Decision for Alex: Not Eligible**

**Reason:** Alex is 17 years old and has started an apprenticeship in England. While Child Benefit can normally continue for children aged 16-19 who remain in approved education or training, the rules specifically state that Child Benefit stops when a child starts an apprenticeship in England. Apprenticeships are not considered "approved education or training" for Child Benefit purposes.

---

I'm sorry the outcome isn't what you may have hoped for. If Alex's circumstances change in the future (for example, if he leaves the apprenticeship and returns to full-time non-advanced education), you may be able to make a new claim at that point.

If you have any questions or would like to discuss this further, please feel free to ask. You can also contact the Child Benefit Office directly if you'd like to discuss your specific situation with them.
